about: A retelling of Zork II territory. You enter a barrow with a lantern and sword and cross a ravine into caverns and a formal garden. A meddling Wizard hints that the treasures lie further south, behind a stone door that asks a question and a room that will not keep still.

done.why: I sampled the opening, the Wizard's illusion and the garden, then stopped at the Carousel Room. I had read enough to rate the writing. I had found no puzzle or ending yet.

moments.note: Turning on the lamp summons the Wizard, whose speech is a wry, characterful hint about where the treasure is.
The jewels are an illusion, and the refusal text is funny: the room 'has the grace to look embarrassed'.
The room 'settles down and is only a room' once the illusion fades.
The newspaper is cleverly adapted to set up the Wizard and the treasures.
The Carousel Room is disorienting with eight identical exits, and I stopped there.

wished: A way to learn what the stone door's question is without a long trek.
To see more of the Wizard's illusions.

lines.line: It has that look of a thing that has been through one adventure already and would rather not discuss it.
lines.why: Sly, affectionate wit about the lantern.

lines.line: the room, having no say in the matter, let it, and has the grace to look embarrassed about it now.
lines.why: Turns a failed take into characterful prose.

lines.line: the public is advised not to let him finish a word.
lines.why: A good joke that also sets up the Wizard's magic.

fun.why: The wit and the illusion gag were charming, though I played only briefly.

engagement.why: Short and curious. The hints pull you south.

difficulty.why: Everything I did was easy, and I never hit a puzzle.

interestingness.why: A familiar world is reworked with new connective tissue, such as the Wizard's illusions and hints.

prose.why: Dry, witty and specific descriptions that reward reading closely.
